propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark invokes author() 6000 times causing 6000+ subprocess-backed git config user.name lookups consuming 47.79s, with only one logical distinct value needed per import

Each CREATE in a batch calls sweep_stale_staging independently, causing 3000 redundant sweeps with 375876 staging-owner checks (15.94s cumulative), when the same staging root could be swept once per batch
Author identity must remain live and re-queried for each independent/interactive write but can be cached within an explicit bounded import context without leaking across calls/threads/sessions

The batch_stage_and_commit path can defer stale sweeps until the first new ticket in each bounded chunk is staged, reducing sweep count from N to N/chunk_size while preserving crash-resume, rollback, and atomic behavior

Controlled identical-state A/B harness with cache and sweep optimizations only reduced wall time 77.231s to 16.404s (-60.8s, -78.8%) while preserving 3000 creates, 3000 comments, 29 commits, and state equivalence

Test contract (N=3000, 6000 events, exactly 24 commits, >=10x reduction, crash-resume, rollback) must remain unchanged; observable postcondition requires exactly one user.name lookup per import and stale sweeps equal half expected commits (12 for current locked contract)
